# A fire-and-forget remote dispatch turns an expected teardown reject into an unhandled-rejection storm

## Context

Successor to #17976, which is closed as premise-falsified. @tobiu reported on 2026-08-31 that opening a built portal emitted the same rejection **thousands of times**:

```
Base.mjs:411  Uncaught (in promise) undefined
(anonymous)         @ Base.mjs:411
promiseMessage      @ Base.mjs:405
(anonymous)         @ RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:164
(anonymous)         @ Body.mjs:1271
Promise.then
onStoreLoad         @ Body.mjs:1270
fire                @ Observable.mjs:284
onCollectionMutate  @ Store.mjs:1082
fire                @ Observable.mjs:284
splice              @ Base.mjs:1608
appendFeedBatch     @ Workspace.mjs:620
```

#17976 attributed this to `neo-config.json`'s `basePath` re-anchoring, and prescribed re-anchoring it into `dist/esm`. That was traced to source and refuted — the module boot chain never reads `basePath`, and the prescribed change would have broken `resourcesPath`, the Font Awesome href and every theme stylesheet root. Full trace on #17976.

**What survives is the storm itself**, which #17976 pushed out of scope as *"the amplifier, not the fault"*. With the fault gone the amplifier is the whole finding, and unlike the fault it is verifiable at source without reproducing @tobiu's session.

*Separated from inference:* the observed operation is a `Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo` dispatch rejecting under a ticking store feed. **Not** established: which context produced @tobiu's specific frames — the trace names `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` while the reported URL is the portal, and #17976 never reconciled that. This ticket claims the mechanism, not that session.

## The Problem

`src/worker/Base.mjs:311` is the reply path:

```js
} else if (promise = action === 'reply' && me.promises[replyId]) {
    if (data.reject) {
        promise.reject(data.data)
    }
```

A remote call therefore *legitimately* rejects — most notably on the dead-port teardown path, where a SharedWorker window has closed and its message port is gone. #17894 deliberately **typed** that rejection so consumers could discriminate expected teardown from real failure. It typed the *reason*. It did not add a *handler*, and the call sites did not grow one.

`src/grid/Body.mjs:1269-1277` is the site in the trace:

```js
if (me.mounted && !postChunkLoad) {
    me.timeout(50).then(() => {
        Neo.main.DomAccess.scrollTo({direction: 'top', id: me.gridContainer.view.id, value: 0, windowId})
    })
}
```

The returned promise is dropped inside a `.then()` callback. When it rejects there is no handler anywhere on the chain, so it surfaces as `Uncaught (in promise)`. `me.timeout(50)` also means the dispatch fires 50ms after the mount check — the window it addresses may be gone by the time the message is sent, which is exactly the condition that produces the typed rejection.

**Why thousands and not one.** `onStoreLoad` runs on every collection mutation (`Store.mjs` → `Observable#fire`), and a ticking feed (`appendFeedBatch` in the workstation workspace) mutates the store on an interval. One unhandled dispatch per tick, indefinitely. The amplification is not incidental — it is what turns a benign teardown race into a console nobody can read, which then hides every real error underneath it.

**The surface is engine-wide, and this ticket does not claim to fix it.** Census on `dev` at 2026-09-01:

| shape | count in `src/**` |
|---|---|
| `Neo.main.<Service>.<method>(` call sites | **97** |
| of those, dispatched inside a `.then()` callback with no `.catch()` | **8** |
| `.catch(` anywhere in `src/**` | 30 |

Most of the 97 drop the promise entirely rather than chaining `.then()`, which is the same defect with fewer frames.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/Base.mjs:398-411` — `promiseMessage()` builds the promise; `:311` rejects it. Both halves are correct and neither is the defect.
- `src/worker/RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:164` — the generated remote stub that returns that promise. It is the seam every one of the 97 sites goes through.
- `src/core/Base.mjs:1172` — `trap(promise)` exists and is adjacent, but is **not** the fix: it registers a destroy-time canceller and **re-rejects**, so a trapped promise still needs a handler. `src/component/Base.mjs:1406/1429/1591` use it correctly, always under `await`.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs:1269` and `src/table/Body.mjs:615` are the same shape in two classes.

## The Fix

Fix the observed storm; do **not** decide the engine-wide contract inside a bug ticket.

1. **The named sites stop being fire-and-forget.** `src/grid/Body.mjs:1269-1277` (and its `src/table/Body.mjs:615` twin) must dispose of the rejection rather than drop it — a scroll nudge into a window that has gone away is an expected outcome, not a failure to report.
2. **The disposition is stated where a reader will meet it.** Whatever handling lands carries a JSDoc clause naming *why* this dispatch may reject and why that is not an error, so the next reader does not re-add a bare `.then()`.
3. **The engine-wide question is routed, not answered here.** Whether the remaining ~95 sites are fixed one by one, whether `RemoteMethodAccess` should dispose of the typed teardown rejection centrally, or whether the engine should grow an explicit fire-and-forget verb is a shaping question with engine-wide blast radius. It belongs in an Ideation Sandbox Discussion, and this ticket deliberately does not pre-empt it.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid.Body#onStoreLoad` scroll dispatch (`src/grid/Body.mjs:1269`) | this ticket | a rejection from the post-timeout `scrollTo` is disposed of at the call site, never left unhandled | none — an unhandled rejection here is the defect | method JSDoc names the teardown reason | negative control: force the dispatch to reject and assert no unhandled rejection reaches the runtime |

| typed teardown rejection (`src/worker/Base.mjs:311`) | #17894 | **unchanged** — the reason stays typed and stays a rejection; this ticket adds handling, it does not silence the producer | n/a | existing | the #17894 arms stay green |
| the remaining ~95 dispatch sites | **not this ticket** | undecided — routed to a Discussion | n/a | n/a | census recorded above so the next owner does not re-derive it |

## Decision Record impact

`none`. No ADR governs remote-dispatch error handling today; if the Discussion in Fix item 3 converges on a central disposition, that is where an ADR would be proposed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A rejecting `scrollTo` dispatch from `grid.Body#onStoreLoad` produces **no** unhandled rejection, proven by an arm that forces the reject path rather than by inspection.
- [ ] The arm is a mutation control both ways: it must go **red** against current `dev`, and it must not pass merely because the dispatch never fired — non-vacuity asserted by observing the dispatch itself.
- [ ] The `src/table/Body.mjs:615` twin carries the same disposition and its own arm; a fix that lands on one and not the other is the shape that let this survive.
- [ ] The typed rejection from #17894 still rejects and still carries its reason — asserted, so "handled" is not silently implemented as "no longer rejects".
- [ ] The census in this body is restated in the PR against the tree it merges into, so the deferred surface is a live number and not a stale one.
- [ ] A Discussion exists for the engine-wide disposition, linked here. This ticket does not wait on it.

## Out of Scope

- The remaining ~95 `Neo.main.*` dispatch sites. Named, counted, deliberately deferred to the Discussion in Fix item 3 — a 97-site sweep inside a bug ticket is how a contract gets decided by whoever happened to be holding the keyboard.
- Changing `promiseMessage` or the `:311` reply path. #17894 settled the producer; this is a consumer defect.
- `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs`'s ticking feed. It is the amplifier's amplifier — it makes one defect visible thousands of times, and it is correct on its own terms.
- Anything about `basePath`, `dist/esm` module resolution, or which tree executes. That was #17976's premise and it is falsified; see its closing comment.

## Avoided Traps

- **Adding a bare `.catch(() => {})`.** It fixes the console and destroys the signal: a real `scrollTo` failure becomes indistinguishable from an expected teardown. The disposition has to discriminate on the typed reason #17894 provides, which is the entire reason that ticket typed it.
- **Reaching for `trap()` because it is nearby.** `core.Base#trap` re-rejects by design (`src/core/Base.mjs:1183`); wrapping the dispatch in it changes nothing about the unhandled rejection and adds a destroy-time canceller nobody asked for.
- **Fixing the amplifier instead of the fault.** Slowing or debouncing the workstation feed would reduce the line count and leave the defect. #17976 already made the mistake of ranking these two; the fire-and-forget dispatch is the fault at any tick rate.
- **Deciding the engine-wide contract here.** 97 sites and a central seam (`RemoteMethodAccess`) is a shaping question. A bug ticket that quietly settles it creates a precedent nobody reviewed.
- **Treating the missing `.catch()` as a style nit.** It is not lint-shaped: the same omission is correct wherever the dispatch cannot reject, and the discriminator is runtime teardown state, not syntax.

AC-6 routed: the engine-wide disposition is now https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/18012 — `Scope: high-blast`, four options in the divergence matrix, each with a falsifier. Peers add rows.

Two notes from implementing your Fix items 1 and 2, both of which changed the shape of the fix:

**A second expected rejection your body did not name.** `core.Base#destroy()` rejects pending timeouts with the `Neo.isDestroyed` sentinel (`core/Base.mjs:516`). Since the dispatch sits behind `me.timeout(50)`, a body destroyed inside that window hits the handler too — so a handler discriminating only on `NEO_DEAD_PORT` would have replaced a rejection storm with an *error* storm, one `console.error` per teardown. Both discriminators have live precedent: `draggable/DragZone.mjs:445` for the dead port, `dashboard/dock/interaction/DockSplitter.mjs:499` for the sentinel.

**The inner promise is not returned** from the `.then()` callback, so appending `.catch()` to the outer chain catches nothing. The dispatch has to be returned into the chain first.

**On the census (AC-5).** I could not reproduce your 97 with any single pattern — I get 49 narrow, 134 wide, 9 for the fire-and-forget shape. I read that as three different questions rather than two-hour drift, so the PR publishes the exact commands instead of quietly replacing your number. One figure does have an internal control: `.catch(` in `src/**` moved 30 → 32, exactly the two handlers added. Your own Avoided Traps line — *"the same omission is correct wherever the dispatch cannot reject"* — is why I think the mechanical census is itself an open question, and it is OQ-3 in the Discussion.
